name: Low-iron float glass
summary: Soda-lime-silica glass melted from low-iron sand and floated on molten tin: clear to the edge, with a pale aqua-blue colour only where light runs a long way through it. It is the museum's glass: the Rotunda's glazed eye, the vitrines, and the glazing of the daylit galleries.

constituents.role: stabilisers: make the glass durable in water
a batch material (SO3 remains in the glass)
an impurity of the sand that sets the colour; low-iron glass keeps it below 100 ppm

formation.how: The batch (sand, soda ash, limestone, dolomite, salt cake and about 20 % cullet) is melted and floated on a bath of molten tin, where it spreads to an even thickness with fire-finished faces; the ribbon is annealed in a lehr and cut. The face that lay on the tin carries diffused tin (the tin side); the other is the air side. Low-iron glass is made the same way from raw materials chosen for their low iron, with the melt's redox held so that little of that iron is ferrous.

edgeColour.description: Pale aqua-blue, seen only through long paths: the edge of a pane, a thick stack, or light running along a pane. Clear float glass is dark green at the edge.
edgeColour.cause: The ferrous band's tail absorbs red about three times as strongly as green or blue, so the least absorbed light is blue-green near 490 nm.

physicalMaterial.note: Friction has no verified source yet (see unverified). The museum's glass is overhead or in vitrines; no floor is glazed.

photograph: The edge: a polished edge, or light running along a pane, is pale aqua-blue; ordinary glass is bottle-green. A green edge means it is not low-iron glass.
Two reflections per pane, one from each face (about 4 % each head-on, rising toward grazing), offset by the thickness; four in an insulating unit. A laminate adds none.
Straight lines in reflection: a slow ripple means reheated (heat-strengthened or toughened) glass; a calm reflection means annealed glass.
Darker patches in polarised skylight or at oblique angles: quench marks of heat treatment.
A grey veil on the weather face of sloped glass, heaviest where water pools against glazing bars, with drainage streaks below them.
Vitrines: a dim, faintly coloured reflection on anti-reflective glass; fingerprints at hand height; a thin interlayer line at a polished laminated edge.
Through the face the view is neutral (Ra 99); under a UV-filtering laminate the light is a touch warmer, because the violet edge is cut.

evidenceSearch.found: No CC0 photograph or PBR set of architectural glass is on this PC. The Albion lancet textures are images of stained-glass designs (Art's), not evidence of this substance; JS4 (ambientCG Rock041) is flint, a glassy stone.
evidenceSearch.tier: Glass is calibrated from tier (a), measured tables (Architecture, Matter: 'Metals and glass are calibrated mainly from (a)'). The spectra and tables in this record are that evidence.
